who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane complexity lints (function_weight .. module_cycle), fix-hello-1113
where: crates/blaze-lints/src/baseline/items.rs (load, Loaded); crates/blaze-lints/src/conf.rs (Conf::items); crates/blaze-cargo/src/compile.rs (`linted`, where `conf.profile` is set); blaze-units (the `lints-ratchet` baselines directory)
what: The complexity lints hold each existing item at its value from crates/blaze-lints/baselines/items.tsv, but the lint crate cannot load the file itself: the build that runs the lints (blaze-cargo's `linted`) is the one place that knows the ratchet's baselines directory and records the files a job looked at, and the lane may not edit it. Until it sets `conf.items = items::load(&baselines, &job.input.looks)?`, every item over a bound is a finding, so the lints stay at `warn`.
cost: the ratchet's per-crate counts and the per-item held values are read in two different places; the lints cannot go to `deny` until a second lane wires the loader and blesses
cause: the lint configuration (Conf) is assembled in the build driver from pieces each lint family adds (the profile, now the held values), so each new input of a lint needs a driver edit outside the lint crate
class: lint inputs that live beside the workspace config but are loaded by the driver one by one
prevention: one loader in blaze-lints, called once by the driver with the ratchet's directory and the job's looks, that fills every file-backed part of Conf (profile, baselines, held values); a new lint input is then a field and a line in that loader
workaround: set `conf.items` in compile.rs next to `conf.profile`, with the directory from `[workspace.metadata.blaze.lints-ratchet] baselines`
